name: Ahikam
source_summary: A court official under King Josiah who was sent to consult the prophetess Huldah about the newly discovered Book of the Law, and who later personally protected the prophet Jeremiah from being put to death by an angry crowd; his son Gedaliah became governor of Judah after Jerusalem's fall.
family_friendly_summary: Ahikam was a trusted official who served King Josiah of Judah. When workers found an old scroll of God's Law hidden in the temple, Josiah sent Ahikam and a few other officials to ask the prophetess Huldah what it meant for the kingdom. Years later, when the prophet Jeremiah gave a hard warning message from God and an angry crowd wanted to kill him for it, Ahikam personally stood up for Jeremiah and kept him safe. Ahikam's son, Gedaliah, later became the governor of Judah after Jerusalem was destroyed by the Babylonians. Ahikam is remembered as a faithful official who respected God's word and protected God's messenger, even when it was risky.
adult_story: Ahikam son of Shaphan served as a royal official during King Josiah's reign. When the Book of the Law was discovered during temple repairs, Josiah sent Ahikam, along with Hilkiah the priest, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah, to inquire of the LORD about it through the prophetess Huldah, who confirmed both coming judgment on Judah and mercy for Josiah personally because of his humble response (2 Kings 22:12-20). Years later, under King Jehoiakim, Ahikam's courage surfaces again: after Jeremiah delivered a temple sermon warning that Jerusalem would become like Shiloh, priests, prophets, and people seized him and demanded his death. Scripture records plainly that "the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah so that he was not given into the hands of the people to put him to death" (Jeremiah 26:24) -- Ahikam's personal intervention is credited with saving the prophet's life. Ahikam's own son, Gedaliah, was later appointed governor over the remnant left in Judah after Jerusalem's fall to Babylon (2 Kings 25:22), though Gedaliah was soon assassinated (Jeremiah 41:1-3). Ahikam's brief but consistent appearances show a court official who used his influence both to seek God's word faithfully and to defend God's messenger at personal risk.
devotionals: When a mob wanted to kill Jeremiah for his hard message from God, Scripture says Ahikam's own hand was what kept the prophet from being handed over to die. Jesus, too, faced a mob demanding His death, but no one stood between Him and the cross, because that death was the rescue we needed.

Ahikam used his influence at court both to seek God's word through Huldah and to protect God's messenger at real personal risk. May we use whatever influence we have that same way, standing up for the truth of Jesus even when it costs us something to do it.
